parts.note: the Picts were ancient inhabitants of Caledonia, the Roman name for Scotland, so a Caledonian can be a Pict
a flower in crosswords is often a river (something that flows); the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A review of a movie about a Scottish bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' tempts as a plant, but it is read as 'something that flows', a river: the Yorkshire Ure.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture is an everyday word for a movie, as in going to the pictures.

parts.note: a perch, also called a rod or pole, is an old unit of length

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters of cane are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fishing rod broke a walking cane by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod' suggests a fishing rod, but it is the old unit of length of the same name; 'damaged' is the anagram signal for the walking stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Perchance is an old-fashioned word meaning by chance or possibly, close to happening accidentally.

clue.text: Father getting up to look both ways at spacecraft

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means rising, so the word for father is read from bottom to top

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: the short word for look is written backwards and then forwards, giving a run that reads the same either way

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Dad rises to check left and right before a rocket launch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting up' turns PA into AP; LO taken 'both ways' gives OL then LO, so OLLO. 'to' and 'at' only link the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollo was the name of the NASA programme and its craft that took astronauts to the Moon.

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the last letter of the word for flexible is dropped

parts.note: supple means flexible or bendy
a worker in crosswords is often an ant, as in a worker ant

explanation.surface: A bendy employee is shunted aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the last letter of the word for flexible; a worker as the insect is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: To supplant someone is to take their place, ousting or replacing them.

clue.text: On which to act without premeditation

definitions.text: On which to act without premeditation

parts.words: On which to act without premeditation
parts.note: the whole clue describes the impulse of an instant that prompts acting with no forethought; the phrase usually follows 'on the'

explanation.definitionFit: A sudden impulse that drives unplanned action, as in doing something on a whim, is this phrase.

clue.text: In which petrol might be waiting to be dealt with

definitions.text: In which petrol might be waiting to be dealt with

parts.words: In which petrol might be waiting to be dealt with
parts.note: fuel literally travels through a long pipe, and a matter 'in the' same pipe is figuratively pending or on its way

explanation.definitionFit: A long pipe for carrying oil or gas, whose idiom 'in the ...' means under way but not yet finished.

indicators.note: struggling suggests thrashing about, so the remaining letters are jumbled
leaving means going away, so these letters depart from the name

parts.note: the clue spells out the two letters E and S

explanation.surface: A Cockney Charles struggles as he leaves for a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes E and S out of CHARLES, leaving CHARL, which 'struggling' rearranges. The apostrophe suggests Cockney 'he's' to hide the plain letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The larch is a deciduous conifer, a kind of tree that sheds its needles in winter.

clue.text: Gear for those not taking sides

definitions.meaning: one setting of a car's gearbox, where the engine turns nothing
describing people or nations who stay impartial

explanation.surface: Equipment designed for people who stay out of arguments.
explanation.definitionFit: Neutral is the gear position with no drive engaged, and also describes being impartial in a dispute, as Switzerland was in wartime.

parts.note: to grant something is to give it
up means raised or increased, as in prices being up

explanation.surface: A grant was raised following a capitulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' here is a link meaning 'leading to'; the two pieces stand in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up is to stop resisting and yield, the same as to capitulate.

clue.text: It's a blow when part of shoe is damaged

parts.note: the upper is the part of a shoe above the sole
cut means slashed or damaged

explanation.surface: Bad news when the top of your shoe gets slashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's a blow' looks like 'what a pity', but the blow is a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: An uppercut is a boxing punch thrown upward at the chin.

indicators.note: inside means one piece sits within the other, so the abbreviation for left goes into the word for label

parts.note: a sticker is an adhesive label

explanation.surface: A pedant is found with a tag stuck inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' is only a link; 'inside' puts the abbreviation for left within the word for label, just before its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler insists on exactness about rules or details, a pedant who fusses.

clue.text: Henry brought back raw material from the city

indicators.note: brought back means returned, so the nickname for Henry is written backwards

parts.note: Hal is a familiar form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
ore is the raw mineral material from which metal is extracted

explanation.surface: Henry returns with raw goods from town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns HAL into LAH; 'from the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lahore is a major city in Pakistan, capital of Punjab province.

clue.text: Stop working for a time although holiday is cancelled

parts.note: a break is a short holiday, as in a city break
off means cancelled, as in the match is off

explanation.surface: Pausing work even though the trip has been called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'although' and 'is' are link words; the definition is the first four words.
explanation.definitionFit: To break off is to pause an activity for a while, like downing tools temporarily.

indicators.note: woolly means fuzzy or muddled, so the letters of the next word are muddled

explanation.surface: A sheep's fleecy bleat is something substantial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woolly' fits the sheep picture but is the anagram signal for BLEATING.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangible means able to be touched, physically real and substantial.

parts.note: 'no end of' seems to mean lots of, but the island's native cat breed has no tail, the end of a cat

explanation.definitionFit: This British Crown dependency in the Irish Sea is home to the tailless Manx cat.

definitions.meaning: a traditional size of writing or printing sheet
headgear placed over a dunce, a slow-witted person

explanation.surface: Newsprint is laid on top of a slow pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old large size of writing paper, and also the pointed hat once worn by a slow pupil.

clue.text: Horrible having become a bit taller, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the phrase is judged by its sound when spoken

parts.note: having grown a little, which can be put as 'grew some'

explanation.surface: Someone finds it horrible to have gained a little height.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grew some' (became a bit taller) sounds like the word meaning horrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruesome means ghastly and repellent, causing horror or disgust.

clue.text: Be accommodating for at least the second time

definitions.text: Be accommodating for at least the second time

parts.words: Be accommodating for at least the second time
parts.note: 'accommodating' looks like being obliging, but it means housing someone; doing so again is the re- prefix

explanation.definitionFit: To give someone new lodging, typically after they lose their home, is to house them again.

indicators.note: embarrassing suggests confusion, so the letters of defeats are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Fans partied after some humiliating losses.
explanation.definitionFit: To have feasted is to have marked an occasion with a banquet.

parts.note: an exclamation of surprise, 'Holy ...!', completed by an oily sea fish with a striped back

explanation.definitionFit: This striped oily sea fish completes the old exclamation of astonishment beginning with 'holy'.

parts.note: 'make light of' looks like belittling, and 'wicked' like evil; it is an object with a wick that gives light

explanation.definitionFit: A wax stick with a wick that burns to give light.

parts.note: 'oratory' seems to be speech-making, but it is a small place of worship, the kind used by Methodists and Baptists

explanation.definitionFit: In Britain, a Nonconformist place of worship such as a Methodist one is called by this name rather than church.

parts.note: the Po is the longest river in Italy
a Lar was a Roman household god

explanation.surface: Someone stands firmly against a river deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word. The Lares were the guardian spirits of a Roman home.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar opposites are exactly contrary, like the two ends of an axis.

clue.text: It is apparent party statement stopped short

indicators.note: stopped short means cut off before the end, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: a political party's published statement of its policies

explanation.surface: Clearly the party's policy document was cut off before the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It is' is a link; 'stopped short' trims the final O from the policy document's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifest means plain to see, obvious and evident.

clue.text: Said twisted rod had ornamental twist

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: a curly cue: a cue is a rod used in snooker, and a twisted one is curly

explanation.surface: Someone reports that a bent stick had a decorative swirl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted rod' gives 'curly cue', which said aloud is the word for a decorative flourish; 'had' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A curlicue is a fancy spiral flourish in handwriting or decoration.

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow or field
a den is a small private room such as a study

explanation.surface: A boring field of study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'field study' reads as one academic subject but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaden means heavy and lifeless, sluggish or dreary, like grey lead.

clue.text: Last month salesman had item in the last stage of decay

definitions.text: in the last stage of decay

parts.note: Dec is the abbreviation for December, the last month of the year
a rep is a sales representative
it is a word for an item, as in a thing

explanation.surface: In December a salesman had a product that was falling apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrepit means worn out and broken down by age or neglect.
